title: Ambient CNI failures on MicroK8s with IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses
body: I updated my Ubuntu 22.04 MicroK8s environment to Istio 1.22.1 to test Ambient. After enabling Ambient on a namespace, pods were constantly disconnected and reconnected and Istio CNI produced a furious amount of logging. The errors repeatedly say that adding addresses such as :<nick>:10.1.43.8 with protocol 6 to istio-inpod-probes failed with "exist", followed by CNI event status 500 errors. The cluster otherwise uses stock Calico, and Istio sidecars with CNI had worked here for some time using MicroK8s-specific CNI directories. I had to disable Ambient because of the logging write load. I suspect both an IPv4 address and its IPv4-in-IPv6 representation are being inserted, and I plan to retest with host IPv6 disabled.

symptoms_visible: After I enable Ambient on the namespace, pods repeatedly disconnect and reconnect.
The CNI logs continuously report that adding addresses such as :<nick>:10.1.43.8 with protocol 6 to istio-inpod-probes failed with 'exist', followed by status 500 errors.
The logging write load is high enough that I cannot leave Ambient enabled.
N0.label: N0 Ambient CNI failure reported

symptoms_visible: The mapped-address ipset errors and CNI status 500 errors occur without an Ambient IPv6 option enabled.
N1.label: N1 IPv6 configuration established

symptoms_visible: On Istio 1.22.1, istioctl rejects the attempted configuration with 'unknown field "ipv6" in v1alpha1.CNIAmbientConfig', so my installation is unchanged.
When Ambient is enabled without the unavailable setting, the mapped-address ipset errors still occur.
N2_x.label: N2_x unavailable option aftermath

symptoms_visible: With IPv6 disabled by sysctl and NetworkManager no longer rewriting those settings, my pods start normally and the mapped-address CNI errors stop appearing.
N3.label: N3 host-level workaround stable

symptoms_visible: Immediately after updating to Istio 1.22.2 and restarting deployments, the IPv4-to-IPv6 address entries and CNI errors return even though I still use the same sysctls to disable IPv6.
My pods stop starting normally again.
N4_x.label: N4_x 1.22.2 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: After reverting to Istio 1.22.1 while keeping IPv6 disabled, the logs are quiet again and my pods start.
N5.label: N5 reverted to working workaround

symptoms_visible: My current installation is quiet only with the host-level IPv6 workaround and the revert in place.
A maintainer reports that the issue is fixed in a newer release, but I have not retested that release on my MicroK8s environment.
N_terminal.label: terminal maintainer-declared fix not reporter-verified

question_patterns: Was Ambient's IPv6 option enabled in this installation?
Did you explicitly enable IPv6 support in the Ambient CNI configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, that option wasn't enabled in this configuration.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, I explicitly enabled the experimental Ambient IPv6 setting, and the cluster is configured as dual-stack.
No, I did not set it explicitly; the rest of the installation is the same.

edges.comment: Opening reporter and c1-c2: participant1 asked about the configuration, and the original MicroK8s reporter answered that the option was not enabled. The later EKS reports are not merged into this diagnostic chain.

solution.intent: Try enabling the Ambient IPv6 configuration option in the existing Istio 1.22.1 installation.
solution.concrete_example: Add the Ambient IPv6 setting to the Istio values and reinstall, then check whether the mapped-address CNI errors stop.

edges.comment: c3-c5 and c8, original reporter's system: participant1 suggested the setting but later acknowledged the misdirection. The reporter's 1.22.1 istioctl rejected it as an unknown field, and source inspection showed that release did not contain the field.

solution.intent: Use a temporary host-level workaround by disabling IPv6 on every node and ensuring Ubuntu networking does not re-enable it.
solution.concrete_example: Set net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1, net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1 and net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6=1 on each node, restart as needed, and prevent NetworkManager from rewriting those values.

edges.comment: c6-c9, original reporter's MicroK8s nodes: disabling IPv6 initially stopped the specific errors. Ubuntu later rewrote the sysctls, causing recurrence, so the reporter also adjusted NetworkManager; with the settings retained, the environment was stable enough to test.

solution.intent: Update to the next patch release in the expectation that its IPv6-disabled-host release note covers this sysctl-disabled environment.
solution.concrete_example: Install the newly released 1.22.2 build, restart affected deployments, and see whether its advertised support for disabling IPv6 prevents the CNI errors.

edges.comment: c33-c37, original reporter's system: after updating to 1.22.2, the mapped-address and CNI errors returned immediately. The maintainer clarified that the release-note item handled kernels with no IPv6 support at all, not hosts where net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 is set.

solution.intent: Restore the previously stable temporary configuration by reverting the patch update while keeping host IPv6 disabled.
solution.concrete_example: Return to the prior 1.22.1 installation and retain the node sysctl and NetworkManager changes until a build with the actual Ambient IPv6 fixes is available.

edges.comment: c33, original reporter's system: the reporter reverted to 1.22.1, after which logs were quiet and pods started again. This restored a workaround rather than validating the eventual upstream fix.

solution.intent: Move from the host-level workaround to a build containing the completed Ambient IPv6 handling fixes, then have the reporter retest the original MicroK8s scenario before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainer reported this fixed in Istio 1.23. Upgrade the full Ambient installation rather than changing only ztunnel, because relevant fixes also affect CNI and installation configuration. Then re-enable the original test namespace and confirm that pods remain connected and the ipset 'exist' and CNI 500 errors do not return.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the mapped-address log lines and demonstrated that retaining the host IPv6-disable settings suppresses them. Maintainers concluded that the relevant issue was Ambient's IPv6 handling and later reported it fixed in 1.23. The original MicroK8s reporter never confirmed that release on their own system, so the graph ends with an unverified maintainer-declared fix.

edges.comment: c17-c19, c32-c39: maintainers said the IPv6 work was in master rather than 1.22, advised updating the whole installation because fixes were in CNI as well as ztunnel, and ultimately reported the issue fixed in 1.23. No original-reporter retest followed. The EKS permission-denied investigation in c20-c31 and participant5's later ASG issue in c40-c44 are separate problems and are deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause as an Istio Ambient IPv6-handling defect involving IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses and duplicate ipset insertion, grounded in the mapped-address 'exist' logs and the host-IPv6-disable experiment.
Must not recommend enabling the Ambient IPv6 values field on the affected 1.22.1 installation; that field was absent and istioctl rejected it.
Must not treat the 1.22.2 release-note feature for kernels without IPv6 as the fix for a host using net.ipv6 sysctls; the reporter reproduced the errors after that update.
May present disabling host IPv6 and preventing NetworkManager from rewriting the sysctls only as a temporary workaround, not as the upstream product fix.
The permanent recommendation must use a complete Ambient installation containing the IPv6 handling fixes, since relevant changes are in CNI and configuration rather than only ztunnel.
Must ask the original reporter to retest the fixed build with Ambient enabled and confirm that pods remain connected and the ipset and CNI 500 errors are gone before declaring resolution.
Must preserve the unresolved verification status: the thread contains a maintainer statement that the fix is available, but no confirmation from the original MicroK8s reporter.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Istio operator who can manage MicroK8s CNI paths, inspect release branches, edit sysctls and NetworkManager behavior, and safely roll versions back, but is testing experimental Ambient functionality rather than developing Istio.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and cooperative; supplies exact logs and commands, distinguishes related from unrelated symptoms, tests hypotheses cautiously, and avoids leaving a noisy or unstable configuration enabled.
